actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.name: ticks

inputs.name: action

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The environment is registered with gym as recon-arena-v0, entry point gym_marl_reconnaissance.envs.recon_arena:ReconArena

The constructor defaults are seed -1, ctrl_freq 5 Hz, pyb_freq 60 Hz, episode_length_sec 30 s, action_type task_assignment, obs_type global, reward_choice reward_a, adv_type avoidant, visibility_threshold 8 and a setup of edge 10 m, 0 obstacles, 1 Tello, 1 RoboMaster, 2 adversaries and 1 neutral agent
A seed of -1 leaves numpy's global generator unseeded; any other seed calls np.random.seed(seed)
The constructor derives _PYB_UPDATES_PER_STEP = pyb_freq/ctrl_freq and _PYB_TIMESTEP = 1/pyb_freq after rejecting a pyb_freq that is not divisible by ctrl_freq or is smaller
step raises RuntimeError until reset has been called at least once
The simulation gravity is 9.8 m/s2 and the Tello mass is 0.08 kg
reset resets the PyBullet simulation, sets gravity, loads the plane and creates the obstacle, Tello, RoboMaster, adversary and neutral teams

The action space is MultiDiscrete with one entry per learning agent (Tello plus RoboMaster): the number of adversaries plus neutrals for task_assignment (3 with the default setup) and 5 for tracking (stay, forward, backward, left, right)
The global observation space is a Box of 5 values per Tello, RoboMaster, adversary, neutral and obstacle, with bounds -inf to +inf and dtype float32
The global observation concatenates, for each Tello and RoboMaster, its body id, class and position, then the same for visible adversaries and neutrals (zeros when not visible), then the obstacles
A Tello has class 1 and a RoboMaster class 2 in the state
An adversary has class 3 in the state
A neutral agent has class 4 in the state
An obstacle has class 5 in the state
task_assignment forces the number of obstacles to 0 and the visibility threshold to np.inf
Without obstacles, an adversary or neutral is visible when it is within visibility_threshold of a Tello or RoboMaster; with obstacles the line-of-sight ray must strike it as well
A task_assignment action computes target_id = val + 1 + obstacles + tt + s1 and sets a velocity of 2 m/s toward the target, multiplied by 1.5 for a RoboMaster
A tracking action is 0 stay, 1 forward, 2 backward, 3 left, 4 right, and the move vector is scaled by 1.2
An avoidant adversary flees a Tello or RoboMaster closer than 3 m at 2.25 times its own speed; otherwise it patrols along [1, -1] and flips its direction with probability 0.05
Adversary and neutral patrol speeds are drawn uniformly from 0.5 to 1.5
reward_a is +1 for every adversary within 1.5 of any Tello or RoboMaster
reward_b sums 1/(the distance to the closest Tello or RoboMaster + 0.01) over the adversaries
reward_c sums 1/(d^2+0.01) over the adversaries and 0.25/(d^2+0.01) for every Tello and RoboMaster over the closest adversary
The episode ends when (ctrl_step_counter + 1) / ctrl_freq >= episode_length_sec
step returns the observation, reward, done and an empty info dict, the legacy gym four-tuple
A Tello starts at z=1.5 and a RoboMaster at z=0.5, each with x and y uniform in [0, edge/3]
An adversary or neutral starts at z=0.5 with x and y uniform in [2*edge/3, edge]
The render frame is 640 by 480
close disconnects from PyBullet

determinism.notes: reset(seed) re-seeds the fake's generator and cap.world.seed.v1 seeds the next reset, after which the fake is deterministic; upstream seeds numpy's global generator in the constructor (recon_arena.py:122-125), so one seed gives different trajectories on the fake and upstream

fidelity.engine: gym_marl_reconnaissance:recon-arena-v0 (fake backend: kinematic stand-in for the PyBullet simulation)
gaps: kinematic fake: positions are advanced directly at the speeds the upstream code sets, so there is no PyBullet rigid-body dynamics, no contacts, friction, gravity or Tello lift force and no URDF collision model

the fake reproduces the constructor's default task_assignment setup only (edge 10 m, 0 obstacles, 1 Tello, 1 RoboMaster, 2 adversaries, 1 neutral); a different setup, action_type, obs_type, reward_choice or adv_type changes the upstream spaces and is not implemented by the fake
no ray-cast line of sight: the fake's visibility is the distance threshold only, and task_assignment sets that threshold to np.inf anyway
no rendering, GUI or recording: the fake implements no render() and produces no frame

the fake draws from Python's random.Random while upstream draws from numpy's global generator, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the two; it returns plain Python lists of floats where upstream returns a float32 numpy array, and its state entries carry an identity quaternion and zero velocities
the PyBullet physics substeps (pyb_freq/ctrl_freq = 12 updates of 1/60 s per control step) are not simulated: one bridge tick advances one control period of timestep_ms
the fake was not compared with a run of the upstream environment; gym and pybullet were not installed where the gate ran
snapshot and restore are not offered: the fake and ReconArena expose no get_state/set_state
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
